6fc0a63dcad44a5acddd26dc1f10e2721e0b3403.summary: A UK government statement, issued through the National Cyber Security Centre (part of GCHQ), attributes early-2021 intrusions via Microsoft Exchange servers to China. It assesses HAFNIUM, associated with the Chinese state, as highly likely responsible. It attributes APT40 and APT31 to the Chinese Ministry of State Security. APT40 targeted maritime industries and naval defence contractors in the US and Europe. APT31 targeted government entities, including the Finnish parliament in 2020. Open-source reporting indicates at least 30,000 organisations were compromised in the US alone.

hedges: The NCSC assessed it was highly likely that HAFNIUM was responsible, which the report presents as an assessment rather than a certainty.
The 30,000 figure comes from open-source reporting, which the report cites as an indication.
The report describes the Exchange attack as highly likely to enable large-scale espionage.
